Definition: Amasa, the name of two Israelites
BiblicalUsage: Two men share the name, and both end badly. Amasa son of Jether, Abigail's son and David's nephew, is made captain of Absalom's host, then captain of Judah's host in his place, and Joab greets him with a kiss and stabs him in the belly; and Amasa son of Hadlai is a chief of Ephraim who stands up to the king of Israel and sends the captives home clothed and fed; the name is the same; the men are not.
TheologicalSignificance: Two men, one name, and the contrast is the lesson: one Amasa is murdered by the man he replaced, and the other stops a king's cruelty with mercy.
